column3: The identical question about not eating is recast from unresponsive guests into a test of idols' incapacity.
Ibrahim's quiet turn to his household and preparation of food form the narrative counterpart to his quiet turn to the idols.
The instruction to speak rightly about vulnerable heirs does not clarify the idol test.
Ibrahim's striking of the idols is the immediate physical continuation of the test begun in the focus.
The following question about why the idols do not speak completes the same test of their responsiveness.
Moses' declaration to Pharaoh does not add to Ibrahim's challenge to idols.

God's creation of both worshipers and their works denies the independent agency presumed for the idols.
Resistance to the declaration that there is no god but God supplies the wider opposition behind idol worship.
The instruction about preserving grain for future eating is unrelated to the idol challenge.

Bringing Ibrahim before the people prepares the public testing of the idols' agency.

God's causing death and life extends the contrast from food to ultimate agency.
